forecaster_note: Waist to occasionally chest high at most breaks, nudging head high on the sets at south magnets in the morning. Slight easing into the afternoon with mostly waist high surf by the day's end. Clean all day with offshores. — Surfline Sydney forecast team

wind.summary: Light W–WNW offshore all day — 8kph at dawn, 12kph with 24kph gusts mid-morning, holding W–WNW into the afternoon. Clean the whole day.

shark.summary: No shark detections, drumline catches or drone sightings anywhere on the Northern Beaches in the last 24 hours. All six SharkSmart feeds read this morning and the SLSNSW drone layer is stamped current, so this is a genuine all-clear.

days.label: Today
days.note: Clean, classic winter set-up — W–WNW offshore all day, 12kph with 24kph gusts, and 236 kJ of mostly S groundswell (4.9ft @ 10s from 188°). That dead-south angle is the catch: it wraps in soft at Dee Why and lights up the south-facing corners instead. Low tide 1:28pm, so the 9am–12pm window sits on a draining tide — right in your slot.

dee-why.window: 9am–12pm on the draining tide. Point corner is the pick — the 9s NE lines are what actually make it here, not the south.

tip.label: Frontside at the Point
tip.text: 236 kJ sounds healthy but 4.9ft of it is 188° dead south, and you know how that wraps in gutless at Dee Why. The 2.5ft @ 9s NE and 1.3ft @ 11s ENE are the ones with a shoulder — sit off the Point, pick the lines with an easterly angle and you get your frontside rights. Everything straight out of the south will be a fat wall.

long-reef.window: 9am–12pm. Biggest and best of the four — it's grabbing the whole south swell Dee Why is missing.

tip.label: The size magnet — go here
tip.text: Long Reef is doubling Dee Why on identical energy because 188° swings straight into it. Chest-to-overhead with clean W offshore is the best combination on the coast today. 10s period means proper spacing, not the 7s slop of the last week — paddle-in speed will be there.

curl-curl.window: 9am–12pm. Best size-to-shape balance if Long Reef is crowded or too much.

tip.label: Pick your bank
tip.text: Sits between Dee Why's shelter and Long Reef's exposure — chest-to-head on a clean 12kph W. At 236 kJ with a 10s period the wave is there; the quality is all bank. Walk to the north end and look before you paddle.

manly.window: 9am–12pm, but it's the smallest by a clear margin. Only if you want an easy one.

tip.label: Backside on the lefts
tip.text: North Steyne is the most sheltered of the four from a 188° swell — thigh-to-stomach and soft. Fine for a mellow paddle on your backhand, but you'd be leaving 3ft of clean wave on the table by not driving 10 minutes north.

days.label: Tomorrow
days.note: Go early. Dawn is gusty offshore (15kph W–SW with 41kph gusts) but it settles by 9am, and the swell has already swung to a short-period 4.2ft @ 7s from 190° — more push, less shape. Winds flip onshore SE from about 2pm and that's the end of it. 8am–11am, no later.

dee-why.window: 8am–11am. Easing and short-period — the ENE 10s underneath is the only thing giving it shape.

long-reef.window: 8am–11am. Again the size pick, but a 7s south means walls and closeouts — take the sets with the ENE 10s under them.

curl-curl.window: 8am–11am. Bank-dependent — could be the best or the worst of the four depending on where the sand is.

manly.window: 8am–10am. Smallest again. Skip unless you want a quick one before work.

days.label: Weekend
days.note: Biggest energy of the week — 341 kJ Saturday off a 6.4ft @ 8s south swell, with a trace of 18s long-period underneath. But the direction is 171°, effectively dead south, and S/SSE winds are onshore from first light both days. Saturday is the better of the two: dawn to 9am before it hits 21kph. Sunday starts at 27kph SSE and never recovers.

dee-why.window: Sat dawn–8:30am only. 171° is your worst angle here — 341 kJ that mostly doesn't translate. Sunday is a write-off.
alerts: Dead-south 171° — energy doesn't reach the bank
S/SSE onshore from first light both days

long-reef.window: Sat 6:30–9am. Takes this direction better than anywhere else on the stretch — head-high-plus before the S wind lumps it up.
alerts: S onshore building to 21kph by midday Sat

curl-curl.window: Sat dawn–9am. Size is there but an 8s period south will close out on anything but a perfect bank.
alerts: Closeout risk on a short-period south

manly.window: Sat early. Most sheltered — smallest, but holds shape longest once the S/SE fills in.
